statement: enforcer-memory's default retrieval path (recall/evidence) is a deterministic keyword matcher with zero network calls and zero model downloads; any embedding-backed retriever (e.g. Qwen-class) is gated behind the optional `embeddings` Cargo feature and ships only as an unimplemented trait seam (EmbeddingRetriever) in this slice.
why: The workpack's long-range plan calls for local embedding/reranker models, but cargo test -p enforcer-memory and cargo build --workspace must be runnable in CI and by every worker without a model runtime or network access. Coupling the default build to a model dependency would make the crate's own gate non-reproducible.
howToApply: Any future PR adding real embedding-backed retrieval to enforcer-memory must land behind the `embeddings` feature flag and must not change the default feature set; tests for the default path must keep passing with zero external dependencies.

statement: The usage-ingestion seam is a plain function (ingest_observation) that other crates call directly, not a trait-object registry or event bus; a clean scan/check/run still calls it and records an Incident with clean=true as negative evidence, because the workpack requires usage itself to equal learning, including the absence of a fault.
why: A registry/event-bus design would add indirection and a second crate dependency surface before any caller exists; a direct function call is the smallest seam that lets arc-15 (scan/check/run) and arc-16 (coordination closeout) start calling it later without enforcer-memory needing to know about them first.
howToApply: When wiring scan/check/run/doctor/closeout to enforcer-memory (tracked as an out-of-scope follow-up from x06), call ingest_observation on every run path, including the clean-result path — do not special-case 'nothing to report' as 'skip recording'.

statement: memory evidence <lessonId> must fail-closed: a lesson with no matching node returns Unknown, and a lesson found but with no incident provenance returns a Chain with has_t0_provenance=false, never a chain that looks complete when it is not.
why: The workpack explicitly requires this instrument to be falsifiable — fabricating a t0 step when none exists would make the learning-evidence curve look better than the real data supports, defeating the point of the proof.
howToApply: Any consumer of enforcer_memory::evidence must branch on EvidenceResult::Unknown vs Chain{has_t0_provenance:false} and surface 'evidence:incomplete' rather than treating a partial chain as full evidence.

statement: This workpack's full acceptance block (KG parity vs codebase-memory-mcp, 100 QA rows, HNSW sidecars, weaver background workers, Qwen embedding + reranker with measured lift, live MCP/CLI tool parity) is a multi-lane, multi-session build, not a single-worker one-pass slice; x06 lane one delivered only the ingest+graph+deterministic-recall+usage-seam+evidence-chain core with real tests, and left the rest as named follow-up scope.
why: Recording this now so a future orchestrator reading proof/memory/x06-feature-parity.json's still-unmet fields does not mistake 'crate exists and its own tests pass' for 'workpack DONE' — the workpack's own capsule says exactly this ('Does not prove... broad DONE unless routed proof says so').
howToApply: Before marking x06 DONE, a follow-up pass must implement: the parity harness against an installed codebase-memory-mcp baseline, the 100-row QA benchmark file, the feature-parity test-matrix rows, and wire the ingest_observation seam calls from arc-15/arc-16 (explicitly out of scope for this lane per its file-ownership limit).

statement: Doc-lane worker reports are not evidence: the QA-250 author claimed 150 rows and cited 5 sample row IDs that were all among the 10 actually-missing rows; it also minted its own (owner-set) marker. Verification must mechanically recount every countable claim and grep the diff for added (owner-set lines (owner-only namespace).
why: Cheap-tier workers produce confident, specific, hallucinated evidence; the only reliable gate is an independent script recount plus a marker-addition diff check.
howToApply: On every doc-lane integration: script-count rows/sums against the spec minimums; reject any diff adding a line containing (owner-set unless the commit is owner-authored; missing-ID lists are computed, then handed back verbatim in the fix-pass prompt.
